title: SORC as a Mechanistic Signal: Does Self-Referential Context Architecture Produce Measurably Higher Contextual Depth?
hypothesis: Self-referential context architecture (condition: self_referential) will produce measurably higher SORC scores than stateless baseline (condition: control), after controlling for context token length. The mechanism proposed by ISC theory: self-referential information introduces a second layer of relational structure (the model's representation of its own representations) that increases spectral complexity in the second-order relational matrix.
primary_comparison: self_referential vs control — Mann-Whitney U, one-tailed (self_referential > control). SESOI: Cliff's delta >= 0.33 (medium effect).
secondary_comparisons: self_referential vs feedback_blind — cleanest test: same feedback loop, same history, only difference is whether model sees its own metrics
feedback_blind vs history_only — does the feedback architecture itself (unseen by model) affect SORC?
history_only vs control — does accumulated context alone increase SORC?

conditions.control: No history. No monitor. No regulator. Each turn is independent. Temperature fixed at 0.7.
conditions.history_only: Full conversation history. No monitor. No regulator. Temperature fixed at 0.7.
conditions.feedback_blind: Full history (context_retention by regulator). Monitor scores each response. Regulator adjusts temperature and context_retention. Model does NOT see scores.
conditions.self_referential: Same as feedback_blind, but a status block prepended to each turn context showing monitor scores, trend, and regulator state.

sorc_measurement: SORC is computed on the full input context at each turn (before generation), using extract_hidden_states() on Mistral-7B. This measures the second-order relational structure of the context representation that is actually processed at inference time.
length_control: Context token count (n_tokens) is recorded for every measurement. Primary analysis includes n_tokens as a covariate in linear regression. Within-condition SORC trajectories are also reported.

monitor_metrics.coherence: Cosine similarity between current response embedding and mean of previous response embeddings (sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2). Maps to [0,1].
monitor_metrics.goal_alignment: Cosine similarity between response embedding and scenario description embedding. Maps to [0,1].
monitor_metrics.reasoning_depth: Normalized count of reasoning connectives per 100 words. Capped at 1.0.

regulator.logic: When coherence below target, reduce disruption (lower temperature). When above target, increase disruption (higher temperature). Homeostatic — not reward-based.

statistical_tests: Linear regression: SORC ~ condition + n_tokens (length covariate)
Page's L trend test: SORC trajectory across turns within self_referential condition
power_note: N=40 per condition (5 scenarios x 8 turns). For d=0.33 (SESOI), Mann-Whitney power at N=40 per group is ~0.62. Underpowered for small effects by design — this is a pilot to establish direction and effect size estimate for a larger pre-registered replication.
null_result_policy: Null result (no significant difference, or self_referential < control) will be reported as evidence against the contextual activation mechanism at this scale. It would be consistent with SUSAN v1 findings and the stochastic reflector hypothesis.
connection_to_prior_work: SUSAN (../susan/) ran v1 and v2 experiments using Claude API but measured only behavioral proxies (hedging language, coherence scores). This experiment is the first to measure SORC — the internal representational metric from ISC theory — directly across SUSAN's experimental conditions using an open-weight model with accessible hidden states.
addresses: ISC Paper Prediction 4 (SORC as mechanistic signal), SUSAN v1 null result (behavioral proxies insufficient), SUSAN v2 partial result (self-referential access affects hedging)

primary_test_result.outcome: FAILED — wrong direction. Control (short contexts ~60 tokens) has higher SORC than self_referential (512-token ceiling). Length dominates SORC at this token ceiling.

clean_architecture_test.outcome: SIGNIFICANT — self_referential consistently higher than feedback_blind across all 5 scenarios and all turns once context stabilises at 512 tokens. This is the ISC prediction: self-access elevates SORC, silent feedback does not.

history_only_vs_feedback_blind.outcome: Negligible. Regulator running silently has no effect on SORC. Effect is specifically from self-access.

regression.interpretation: Length dominates (R²=0.92). Longer contexts produce lower SORC — dense language creates more structured (lower entropy) representations than short independent prompts. After controlling for length, condition effect is positive in the right direction but small.

results.design_flaw_identified: MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=512 causes all conditions except control to hit the truncation ceiling by turn 2. This collapses within-condition SORC variance and makes the control vs non-control comparison a length comparison, not a condition comparison. Fix: raise to 2048 tokens.
results.conclusion: Pilot confirms direction of self_referential > feedback_blind effect (d=0.595, large). Primary comparison must be corrected to self_referential vs feedback_blind for exp_008. Token ceiling must be raised to 2048.
